# 1 Enoch Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of the Watchers

---

**1** Observe how the trees cover themselves with green leaves and bear fruit; therefore consider and know with regard to all His works, and recognize how He who lives forever made them thus.

**2** And all His works proceed from year to year forever, and all the tasks they accomplish for Him never change; but as God has ordained, so it is done.

**3** And behold how the sea and the rivers likewise accomplish their tasks and do not change from His commandments.

**4** But you — you have not been steadfast, nor have you done the commandments of the Lord, but you have turned away and spoken proud and insolent words with your unclean mouths against His greatness. O hard-hearted ones, you shall find no peace.

**5** Therefore you shall curse your own days, and the years of your life shall perish, and the years of your destruction shall be multiplied in eternal cursing, and you shall find no mercy.

**6** In those days you shall make your names an eternal curse to all the righteous, and all who curse shall curse by you, and all the sinners and godless shall invoke execration by you.

**7** But for the elect there shall be light and joy and peace, and they shall inherit the earth.

**8** And then wisdom shall be bestowed upon the elect, and they shall all live and shall sin no more through ungodliness or pride; and those who are wise shall be humble.

**9** And they shall transgress no more, neither shall they sin all the days of their life, nor shall they die through the wrath of God; but they shall complete the number of the days of their life, and their lives shall increase in peace, and the years of their joy shall be multiplied in eternal gladness and peace, all the days of their life.

---

*LOGOS notes: Chapter 5 is the rhetorical climax of the nature discourse, turning from observations of creation (chs. 2–4) to direct accusation of sinners (vv. 4–6) and promise to the elect (vv. 7–9). The pivot at v. 4 ("But you...") is a key structural marker preserved in the translation.*
